title: Retry failed webhook deliveries
tldr: Failed deliveries now retry with capped exponential backoff, every attempt is recorded, and operators can list and replay failed deliveries.

risk.why: Changes the delivery worker's ack path; a bug here drops or duplicates events.

ask: Approve the backoff caps (30s base, 1h cap, 8 attempts); check the migration is reversible.
overview: Before this change a failed delivery was acked and dropped. Now the worker records every attempt, hands failures to a retry scheduler that re-enqueues them with capped exponential backoff, and gives up after 8 attempts. Operators get a page listing failed deliveries with a replay button. Read the worker first: everything else hangs off its new ack path.

sections.title: Worker ack path
sections.summary: The worker no longer acks failed deliveries: it records the attempt, then either nacks the job with a backoff delay or, once attempts run out, acks it as permanently failed.

blocks.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Q as Delivery queue
  participant W as Worker
  participant D as Customer endpoint
  participant A as Attempts table
  participant R as Retry scheduler
  Q->>W: receive job (attempt n)
  W->>D: POST event
  D-->>W: 503
  W->>A: record attempt n (status 503)
  W->>R: Next(n, now)
  alt attempts left
    R-->>W: at = now + jitter(min(30s·2ⁿ, 1h))
    W->>Q: nack(job, at)
  else exhausted
    W->>Q: ack (failed permanently)
  end

blocks.md: **Ack ordering.** If recording the attempt fails, the worker returns without ack or nack, so the queue redelivers after its visibility timeout. That keeps at-least-once delivery but can send the same event twice. Destinations already dedupe on `event_id`.

notes.note: 429 now counts as a retryable failure, same as 5xx and network errors.
No ack when the attempt can't be recorded: the queue redelivers (at-least-once).
Nack with a delay is how the backoff is applied; the queue holds the job until `next`.
The success-path record error is ignored on purpose: the event was delivered, history is best-effort.

blocks.md: The constructor grew three dependencies; wiring in `cmd/relay` is unchanged because it builds the worker through `delivery.New`, which already had them.

sections.title: Retry scheduler
sections.summary: New `RetryScheduler`: capped exponential backoff with full jitter. Defaults are 30s base, 1h cap, 8 attempts, so a destination that is down for about 2 hours still gets every event.

blocks.md: Full jitter (uniform in `[0, d)`) over equal jitter: it spreads a burst of failures from one outage better, at the cost of an occasional very short first retry.

questions.why: Matches the plan and keeps the queue small; per-destination config can come later without a migration.

sections.title: Attempts table
sections.summary: One row per delivery attempt, plus a `last_status` column on `deliveries` so the failed list doesn't need a join. The down migration drops both.

sections.summary: Three Prometheus counters (delivered, retried, exhausted) so the retry rate is visible. Not in the plan; added because the alert in the plan needs a signal.

sections.summary: `GET /deliveries` takes a `status` filter, and two endpoints are new: attempt history and replay. The old retries doc, which told destinations to poll, is deleted.

blocks.md: Replay doesn't check whether the delivery is actually failed; replaying a delivered event sends it again. Fine for operators, but worth a guard before this is exposed to tenants.

sections.title: Failed deliveries page
sections.summary: A new page at `/deliveries/failed` lists failed deliveries with a Replay button; replayed rows disappear from the list.

notes.note: Optimistic removal after replay; a failed replay leaves the row (the finally only clears busy).

items: Point a destination at a server returning 503; see attempts 0..7 in `delivery_attempts` with growing gaps.
After the 8th failure the delivery shows on /deliveries/failed.
Replay it with the server back up; it is delivered and leaves the list.
Run the down migration on a copy of prod; the worker still starts on the old binary.
